summary: The earlier findings are fixed. The proxy no longer sets undefined headers, and the host token now comes from the running process. The new temp tests cover token injection, forged-header stripping for HTTP and WebSocket, the tool denylist through the router, and every sync access mode. The change is not ready: the new durable control-plane test fails with 503 instead of 200, and the reindented `connect` sync handler has no test.

findings.body: The new durable test "workspace gateway strips forged extension authority" fails: `expected 503 to be 200` (.tmp-tests/report/durable.log). The gateway returns 503 when `this.workspace.getConnection(session.user.id)` is undefined or an error (apps/control-plane/src/workspace/proxy.ts:109-117). The workspace connection is therefore not ready after `authenticatedRpc.workspace.ensure()`, or this fixture does not set it up. As a result, the test never reaches the header-stripping code, and proxy.ts:280-283 stays uncovered. Wait for the workspace to become ready, or follow the setup of the other gateway tests that pass (for example the `/workspace/rpc/connect` tests near line 4900), so the forwarded `/headers` response is actually checked.

The `connect` procedure now goes through the new access middleware, but no test calls it successfully, so lines 46-72 are uncovered. The only check of `/sync/connect` expects 403 for an actions-only visitor. Add a temp test where an allowed caller (a read-only public visitor and/or the owner) opens `connect` and receives the `{ type: "ready" }` event. That proves the middleware lets reads through and the moved handler still works.

testRequests.rationale: This is an anti-spoofing invariant at the public gateway. It needs a durable guard, and that guard must actually pass.
